title: The landing's loader is honest and short, and shows once per deploy
body:
Author's rule (2026-10-26): a loader only if loading needs it, kept under ~3 s; a blocking percentage loader becomes the visit's remembered negative peak. So main.ts loader() shows REAL progress (fonts, the load event capped at 5 s, each chapter's init a frame apart, ScrollTrigger.refresh(), two painted frames), no minimum time, no fake timer; the hero's entrance plays as the mark leaves. Skipped on reduced motion and with ?nointro.
Frequency, decided 2026-10-29 ('cuanto menos aparezca mejor'): once per DEPLOY. src/lib/landing-head.ts writes the inline head script: it stamps <html data-build> with the deploy id (CF_PAGES_COMMIT_SHA, 'local' otherwise) and adds class 'seen' before the first paint when localStorage 'landing:loader' already holds that id, so the loader never flashes (v2.css) and main.ts skips it; main.ts writes the id when the loader finishes. A new deploy shows it once more. Assets are already cached under hashed names, so a return visit downloads only what changed; do not add a service worker for that. No storage (private mode) just means the loader shows again.
not_derivable: The once-per-deploy rule and why the flag is read in the head script (no flash) are the author's call and a timing constraint the code does not state as a requirement.
